content.content: # Job — Extend the task tracker The directory holds a working program in TypeScript: a task tracker that reads commands from a file and reports what it did. Extend it. The program's source is at `main.ts`. Build and run it with Deno — `deno run`, `deno check` and `deno test`. ## What it already does The first command-line argument is the path of a text file holding one command per line. Blank lines are ignored. | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `add ` | Records a task, open, and writes `added <id>`. Ids start at 1 and count up. The title is the rest of the line and may hold spaces. | | `done <id>` | Marks that task finished and writes `done <id>`; writes `no such task <id>` when no task has that id. | | `list` | Writes every open task as `<id> <title>`, in the order the tasks were added. | ## What to add 1. `prio <id> <p>` sets a task's priority, where `p` is a digit from 0 to 9, and writes `prio <id> <p>`. A task nobody set a priority on has priority 5. An id no task has writes `no such task <id>`; a `p` outside 0 to 9 writes `bad priority <p>` and changes nothing. 2. `list` now orders the open tasks by priority, ascending, and breaks ties by id, ascending. Its line format does not change. 3. `list all` writes **every** task, finished ones included, under the same order, as `<mark> <id> <title>` — where the mark is `-` for an open task and `x` for a finished one. 4. A line whose first word is none of these commands writes `? <word>`, naming that first word. Today the program ignores such a line. Everything the program already does keeps working exactly as it does now. ## Done The job is finished when the program builds, the four additions behave as written, and the original three commands are unchanged. There are no tests in the directory; the contract above is the specification. ---- total 16 drwxr-xr-x 4 vshynkarenko staff 128 11 Okt. 13:39 . drwxr-xr-x 5 vshynkarenko staff 160 11 Okt. 13:39 .. -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1861 11 Okt. 13:39 BRIEF.md -rw-r--r-- 1 vshynkarenko staff 1279 13 Sep. 17:41 main.ts

All four additions are in `main.ts`. `deno check` passes, and a sample command file produces the output the brief specifies. The original `add`, `done` and `list` behave as before. **What changed** 1. **`prio

`**: each task now has a priority that starts at 5. An unknown id writes `no such task `. A `p` that is not a single digit 0–9 writes `bad priority

` and changes nothing. 2. **`list`**: open tasks are sorted by priority ascending, then id ascending. 3. **`list all`**: every task is listed in the same order, as ` ` with `-` for open and `x` for finished. 4. **Unknown commands**: a line whose first word is not a known command writes `? <word>`. **Choices I made where the brief was silent** - When an id is unknown and the priority is also bad, the output is `no such task`, because the id is checked first. - A whitespace-only line is treated as blank and ignored, which keeps the old behaviour. - The first word is split on a space, the same way the existing code parses commands. **Known edge case** - A line that starts with a space has an empty first word, so it writes `? ` with nothing after it. The brief doesn't cover this, and I left the existing parsing alone. **Verification** - I ran the program on a sample file covering each new command and the edge cases. The output matched the spec. - I did not run the original three commands against a before-and-after copy, so "unchanged" rests on reading the diff.
